static_traits.name: Li Sha
static_traits.educational_background: Graduated with a university bachelor's degree
static_traits.family_status: Father used to work at a bank
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received psychotherapy or treatment for psychological problems; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Slightly nervous; clear expression, able to describe negative automatic thoughts concretely; good cooperation; neutral attitude; tending toward self-criticism and overthinking

basic_info.main_problem: When making a mistake at work (especially miscounting change for customers), feeling 'I am an idiot', accompanied by strong anxiety and self-criticism.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizes self-critical thoughts are affecting work performance and overall physical and mental health; hopes to reduce their impact.
growth_experiences: Father used to work at a bank, related to the client's current work environment, but the specific impact has not yet been detailed.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent / not suited for this job

special_situations.event: Making change errors for customers at the counter
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake at work, it means I am not smart and have no ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly checks work and takes deep breaths to relieve tension
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am an idiot; I should not work at a bank

special_situations.event: Making a mistake in front of customers or colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake in front of others, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: More cautious, tries to avoid talking about work-related distress in social settings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am stupid

special_situations.event: Colleagues joking after a work mistake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' jokes mean they think I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling self-criticism to show correction, over-apologizing on the spot
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are mocking me, seeing through my incompetence

special_situations.event: Lying in bed after work recalling the day's mistakes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must be absolutely accurate, otherwise I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive pursuit of perfection in subsequent work, persistent negative self-labeling
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just no good; I will not get better like this

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as capable, recognized as a reliable employee
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged by others as stupid or incompetent
defense_goal: Maintaining control and avoiding mistakes and being devalued through harsh self-criticism and double-checking

object_relations.self_representation: An error-prone, low-ability employee needing to constantly prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges (customers/colleagues) who mock or look down on me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When a work error occurs in front of customers or colleagues, or colleagues joke about the error
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other will look down on me, thinking I am stupid (transference: projecting inner self-denial onto others' evaluation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Over-interpreting or apologizing in a defensive tone, emphasizing one's inadequacy, trying to gain safety through self-deprecation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others or the counselor propose more balanced views and invite them to refute self-labels with evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Positive reframing feels forced; mistakes are the more 'real' evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on rebutting with the argument 'if I were smarter I would not make mistakes', in a restrained but firm tone, repeatedly citing errors as evidence.

manifestations: Tightly binds self-worth to 'absolute accuracy' performance at work
Generalizing one error into the global 'I am stupid / incompetent'
Making a mistake in front of others immediately triggers strong shame and self-deprecation
outcomes: Disturbed sleep, difficulty focusing on self-care

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-blame and self-labeling after a work mistake ('I am an idiot')
In sessions expresses 'feeling strained', cautious about change
Believing one should not work at a bank, tending to limit one's own choices

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believes customers or colleagues must be thinking 'she is stupid'
Interprets colleagues' jokes as negative evaluations of own ability

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Knowing friends are supportive yet unwilling to discuss work troubles
Turns the impulse to express and seek support into pressure and harshness toward oneself

exception_events.target_problem: When facing high-accuracy demands of financial transactions with customers or colleagues present, the client usually experiences strong anxiety and self-criticism, affecting work performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the first few months of working at the bank, the client handled work tasks fairly well, was not trapped by self-criticism, and performed stably overall.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: successful experiences and positive evidence existed in the early-employment stage, so negative automatic thoughts had not yet formed or were less intense then.

positive_force: Having college education and good early-employment performance (evidence of ability and success exists)
Has a supportive network of friends (though not yet used)
Able to clearly identify and express negative automatic thoughts
Has tried self-regulation strategies (repeated checking, deep breathing)
Willing to accept and practice evidence testing and cognitive restructuring
negative_force: Self-evaluation marked by overgeneralization and black-and-white thinking (one mistake means 'I am stupid')
Mind reading and personalization, overly concerned with others' views
The value condition of work being 'absolutely accurate' leads to perfectionist pressure
Anxiety and sleep disturbances weakening recovery and focus
Tense relationships with colleagues, avoiding support (not discussing with friends)

target_behavior.behavior: Strong anxiety and self-deprecation after making a mistake at work (repeatedly self-labeling 'I am stupid / incompetent')
antecedent: Errors occur when giving customers change or handling financial transactions
In situations with customers or colleagues present
Work pressure under high accuracy demands
target_behavior.core_reason: Binds self-worth absolutely to work performance and is excessively harsh toward himself over the long term; the high accuracy pressure of financial transactions becomes a marked trigger
target_behavior.function: Tries to avoid making mistakes again through self-criticism and excessive caution, to gain a sense of control and escape the threat of being negatively evaluated by others
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety intensified, sleep disturbance, difficulty focusing on self-care; tense relationships with colleagues; work performance affected
